properties.snippet: Point locations for visitor-facing recreation assets across Tennessee State Parks, including amenities, access points, trails, and interpretive features. This is a non-editable layer, built from the internally editable Recreation Assets layer.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service contains recreation asset locations for Tennessee State Parks. It represents public-facing park amenities and points of interest that support visitor experiences across the state park system.

Layer
  • Recreation Assets — A statewide point layer of park assets and visitor-use features, including amenities, trails, access points, interpretive features, recreation facilities, and other items associated with park access and enjoyment.
Use Cases
  • Supporting park visitor information and wayfinding.
  • Providing reference data for recreation planning and asset management.
  • Supplying locations that can be used in public park web maps and mobile applications.
  • Helping staff maintain a consistent inventory of visitor-facing park assets.
Geographic Coverage

The service covers Tennessee State Parks across the state of Tennessee.

properties.snippet: Official boundaries for all State Forests managed by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). This is the authoritative dataset for TDF-managed forest lands.
properties.description:
Tennessee State Forest Boundaries

Overview

This feature layer represents the official and authoritative boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). The polygons in this dataset delineate the properties managed by the TDF for sustainable forestry, wildlife habitat, soil and water conservation, and public recreation.

This dataset is intended for use in planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. It serves as the primary GIS data source for all TDF-managed forest properties.

Feature Layer

  • Tennessee State Forest Boundaries: This polygon layer represents the official boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry. 

Data Attributes

  • StateForestName: The common name of the State Forest.
  • AbbrCode: The abbreviated codes.
  • County: The county(ies) that the State Forest is located in.
  • District: The TDF Administrative District that the State Forest is located in.
  • Acres: The calculated acreage of the property.
  • Latitude: Latitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • Longitude: Longitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • YearEst: The year that the State Forest was established.
  • Notes: Additional notes.
  • CollectionMethod: The method of boundary delineation.
  • Hyperlink: The hyperlink to the State Forests' webpage.

Data Maintenance

This layer is actively maintained by the TDF Forest Data and Analysis Unit. It is updated periodically to reflect new acquisitions, boundary surveys, and other administrative changes.

properties.snippet: Public trail representations managed by the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation for all TDEC public properties, with trail attributes for route type, surface, access use, difficulty, and park or natural area association.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides public trail representations managed by the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC). It supports reference, planning, and map display workflows for trail resources across Tennessee state parks and natural areas.

Content

The service includes trail geometry and supporting attributes that describe trail names, trail segments, route type, trail status, surface characteristics, allowed uses, blaze color, difficulty, and park or natural area association. The information captures trail segments for hiking and other recreational uses, including paved, gravel, natural, mulch, water, and riverbed surfaces, along with access categories such as biking, mountain biking, paddling, equestrian use, climbing, wheelchair access, all-terrain wheelchair access, fitness features, and storybook trails.

Coverage

The data covers Tennessee conservation and recreation lands, including state parks, state historic parks, state archaeological parks, state natural areas, and related protected sites managed by TDEC.

Use Cases

  • Trail browsing and recreation planning
  • Park and natural area reference mapping
  • Trail condition and route characterization
  • Outdoor access and accessibility mapping
  • Visitor information support for Tennessee state lands

Data Notes

Representations of trails managed by the State of Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC). This data is updated on an irregular basis. This information has been compiled by TDEC from a variety of sources and is subject to change without notice. TDEC makes no representations as to accuracy, completeness, timeliness, or rights to the use of such information. These data are not intended for use as a survey product. TDEC shall not be liable for any general, special, indirect, incidental or consequential damanges including but not limited to: lost revenues or lost profits resulting from the use or misuse of the information contained in this data. Any sale of this data is prohibited except by written permission of TDEC.

properties.snippet: This service features detailed data on Tennessee marinas, including amenities, parking, and access information for statewide recreational use.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides comprehensive data on marinas located throughout the state of Tennessee. It is designed to support recreational boating and fishing activities by offering detailed information about facilities and amenities available across various public access points to waterways.

Feature Layer: Marina Sites

This primary layer represents individual marina locations. It includes detailed attributes such as geographic coordinates, county, associated waterway, and site name. The layer categorizes sites with descriptors for parking availability and surface type, hours of operation, and access fees, enhancing usability for public and agency personnel.

Key features covered include:

  • Location and type of access sites such as boat launches, marinas, and fishing sites.
  • Parking details including surface type and capacity, including trailer parking.
  • Facilities and amenities like gas availability, ice, bait, camping, restrooms, fishing piers, fish cleaning stations, and courtesy docks.
  • Operational considerations such as access hours, seasonal closures, and 24-hour availability.
  • Site ownership and management information by various government and private entities.
  • Accessibility features including handicap and lighted parking.
  • Restrictions or special conditions such as trolling-only areas or rental availability.

Geographic Coverage

The dataset covers the entire state of Tennessee, with sites organized by county and waterway, providing statewide access to boating facilities.

Use Cases

  • Planning and management of recreational boating and fishing infrastructure by state and local agencies.
  • Providing the public with detailed site information for trip planning and safe boating access.
  • Supporting emergency response and maintenance scheduling for water access points.

properties.snippet: This service maps fishing access sites across Tennessee, detailing facilities and amenities at each location.
properties.description:
Overview

This Feature Service provides comprehensive information on fishing access locations throughout Tennessee, specifically highlighting boat ramps, marinas, and fishing sites.

Feature Layer

  • Fishing Sites: This layer features detailed data on Tennessee Fishing Sites. It includes geographic locations, regional and county identifiers, and information about waterways. The layer offers extensive attributes related to parking facilities, ramp structures, availability of amenities like ice, bait, and camping, and the management and ownership of the sites. It also covers accessibility features such as four-wheel drive access, handicapped parking, and lighting. Operational details such as hours open, access fees, and seasonal closures are recorded, along with details about boating suitability, including launchable boat sizes and types of vessels allowed.

Geographic Coverage

The service covers a broad area within Tennessee, encompassing multiple counties throughout the state, providing a statewide perspective on recreational boating and fishing locations.

Use Cases

  • Supporting recreational boaters and anglers in locating and accessing boat ramps and fishing sites.
  • Assisting resource managers and local authorities with site management and facility planning.
  • Facilitating tourism and outdoor recreational activity planning in Tennessee.

properties.snippet: Tennessee soil units derived from gSSURGO dataset published by the USDA. This is a TDF authoritative dataset for statewide soils.
properties.description:
Tennessee gSSURGO Soils

Overview

This feature layer represents the authoritative statewide soil units derived from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Gridded Soil Survery Geopgraphic database (gSSURGO). The polygons in this dataset delineate the boundaries of soil units for use in assisting sustainable forestry, wildlife habitat, soil and water conservation, and public recreation.

This dataset is intended for use in planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. It serves as the primary TDF GIS data source for Tennessee soils.

Data Attributes

  • AREASYMBOL: The state area symbol of the mapunit.
  • SPATIALVER: The spatial version of the mapunit.
  • MUSYM: The abbreviated symbol of the soil mapunit.
  • MUKEY: The mapunit key field is found throughout SSURGO and provides a primary link between the geographic and tabular data.
  • MUNAME: The full mapunit name.
  • FARM: The farmland classification of the mapunit.
  • ACRES: Acreage of the mapunit.
  • HYDRICRATING: The hydric rating of the mapunit.
  • LCPRIMARY: The primary land cover classification of the mapunit.
  • LCSECONDARY: The secondary land cover classification of the mapunit.
  • DRAINAGECLASS: The drainage class of the mapunit.
  • HYDROGROUP: The soil hydrologic group code of the mapunit.
  • FROSTFREEDAYS: Number of frost free days in a calendar year, on average, of the mapunit.
  • SOILORDER: The taxonomic soil order of the mapunit.

Data Maintenance

This layer is actively maintained by the TDF Forest Data and Analysis Unit. It is updated periodically to reflect new data publishes from the gSSURGO dataset.
properties.licenseInfo:

Soil Survey Staff. Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) Database for Tennessee. United States Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Conservation Service. Available online at https://gdg.sc.egov.usda.gov/. November 17, 2025 (FY2025 official release).

Maintained by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF) - Forest Data and Analysis Unit.

The information is provided “as is” without warranty or guarantee of any kind as to its accuracy, content, completeness, legality, or reliability. The TDF, its employees, agents, and contractors assume no liability for the improper or incorrect use of this data.

NRCS Regulatory Limitation

This dataset is not designed for use as a primary regulatory tool in permitting or citing decisions but may be used as a reference source. Federal, State, or local regulatory bodies are not to reassign to the Natural Resources Conservation Service of the Tennessee Division of Forestry any authority for the decisions that they make.

Mapping Scale Warning

Photographic or digital enlargement of these maps to scales greater than at which they were originally mapped can cause misinterpretation of the data. If enlarged, maps do not show small areas of contrasting soils that coule have been shown at a larger scale.
